root_cause.text: `f2fs_finish_read_bio()` called `f2fs_sanity_check_node_footer()` on node folios without first verifying that the BIO read succeeded, so it could inspect uninitialized folio contents when device I/O failed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (bio->bi_status == BLK_STS_OK && F2FS_F_SB(folio)->node_inode && is_node_folio(folio) && f2fs_sanity_check_node_footer(...))`, and the CVE report says “we may access uninit data in folio if we failed to read the data from device into folio.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: `f2fs_finish_read_bio()` called `f2fs_sanity_check_node_footer()` on node folios without first verifying that the BIO read succeeded, so it could inspect uninitialized folio contents when device I/O failed.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (bio->bi_status == BLK_STS_OK && F2FS_F_SB(folio)->node_inode && is_node_folio(folio) && f2fs_sanity_check_node_footer(...))`, and the CVE report says “we may access uninit data in folio if we failed to read the data from device into folio.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid overwrite of an existing bio error by only performing node footer validation on successful reads.
intent_record.what: In f2fs_finish_read_bio(), the condition that triggers a node footer sanity check was extended with an additional leading test: `bio->bi_status == BLK_STS_OK`. The rest of the conditional logic remains unchanged, and the assignment of `bio->bi_status = BLK_STS_IOERR` is still performed only inside that block.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the node footer sanity check now runs only when the bio has not already failed. This prevents overriding an existing I/O error status with a footer-sanity-derived error, preserving the original failure state while still allowing the footer check to mark a previously successful read as failed if corruption is detected.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid overwrite of an existing bio error by only performing node footer validation on successful reads.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds a success check before validating the node footer, preventing inspection of folios after a failed BIO read and avoiding overwriting the existing I/O error.

candidates.rationale: This is the node-footer validation call that was performed without first checking whether the BIO read succeeded. On read I/O failure, the folio contents may be uninitialized, so invoking this check can inspect invalid data and trigger incorrect error handling.

vuln_statements.explanation: This node-footer validation was executed before verifying that the BIO read succeeded. If the device I/O failed, the folio contents could be uninitialized, so calling this check could inspect invalid data and lead to incorrect error handling.
